A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 30-page versions of GOLD, including Appendices A.1–A.13. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish correspondence of the equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GOLD evaluations on five graph datasets, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and computational measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original GOLD benchmark results, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and computational measurements reported in v1.

M1.justification: GOLD's architecture, generators, alternating optimization, and intended objectives remain unchanged. The corrected softmax indexing matches v1's existing explanation and expanded probability expressions; it does not establish a changed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Twitch, Cora, Amazon-Photo, Coauthor-CS, and ogbn-Arxiv with the same regional, structural, feature, label, and temporal OOD scenarios (Section 4; Appendix A.6).

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1 and the appendix comparisons, including the GNNSafe and NodeSafe variants evaluated with additional backbones in Table 23.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, evaluation metrics, model configurations, training settings, and testing procedures are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A.6–A.8, A.11, and A.13.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component and regularizer ablations, adversarial-training comparisons, energy visualizations, hyperparameter sensitivity studies, and additional-backbone analyses. None is added, removed, or revised.

E5.justification: The uncertainty reporting in Table 1 and Tables 11–15 is unchanged, including Table 1's explanation of variability across test sets. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative experimental findings are retained, including appendix results and computational measurements. For example, Table 1 reports GOLD with LDM achieving Twitch AUROC 99.46% and FPR95 1.78% in both versions.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the stated detector coding from ID=0/OOD=1 to ID=1/OOD=0, aligning it with Equation 3. Equation 10 and Appendix A.1, Equations 16 and 18, correct softmax application from phi(logits[k]) to phi(logits)[k]. These are limited formal corrections; Proposition 1 and the proof's substantive argument remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims: implicit adversarial pseudo-OOD generation for graph detection without auxiliary OOD data or pretrained generators.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, dataset-specific interpretations, and limitations remain unchanged. These include dependence on classifier quality, generative-training costs, node-level applicability, and limitations of energy regularization.

D1.justification: The implementation details, hyperparameter ranges, software versions, hardware, computational measurements, and code/data access information are unchanged, including the reproducibility statement and appendix disclosures.

R1.justification: Section 5, Appendix A.3, and the references retain the same cited works and positioning relative to non-exposure detection, real OOD exposure, and OOD generation methods.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the detector convention, mathematical notation, and arXiv version/date stamp. The paragraphs, section organization, terminology, and narrative structure are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–23 retain their displays, captions, structures, and placement. There is no figure or table redesign or page-layout reorganization.

improvement.justification: v2 removes a detector-label inconsistency in Section 2 and corrects malformed softmax expressions in Equation 10 and Appendix A.1. This improves mathematical clarity and internal consistency. The benefit is limited: the intended method, substantive proof argument, empirical evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
